content:
I'm writing this article and about to head off on a short trip up north. Every time I leave, there are a few essential devices in my smart home system that I rely on completely to make sure everything runs smoothly. Quick reminder: to control your devices remotely and use all the features below, you'll need a dedicated Apple Home hub, such as an Apple TV 4K or HomePod.

The "HomeKit Weekly" series covers smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Outdoor watering system automation

Where I live, it gets ridiculously hot. I suppose when you're not at home, you'd want it to rain — otherwise you have to water the plants yourself. If you're travelling in summer, automatic watering is definitely one of the simplest and most practical smart home applications. If you've ever come back from a week away to find a patch of lawn or a few potted plants completely dead, you'll know exactly what I mean. There are plenty of smart products on the market that connect directly to your tap, letting you turn on sprinklers manually or set up automations based on specific times and local weather conditions.

Step into a comfortable temperature the moment you get home

Coming back from a long trip to find the whole house hot and stuffy, with the air conditioning having been on for ages but still not cool — that's the worst experience. On the flip side, leaving the AC running for hours to keep an empty house at a set temperature is just a waste of money. With a smart thermostat that supports Apple Home, you can remotely adjust the cooling to your preferred temperature the night before. I've been using this approach for a few years now. I prefer turning the AC on at night so the unit can bring the temperature down during the coolest part of the day. This saves money and reduces unnecessary wear on the air conditioner.

Automatic lights on and off to give the impression someone's home

One of the most traditional burglary-deterrent methods is to leave a few lights on so the house looks occupied. The problem is, if the same light is on day and night, you're basically telling people no one's home. This is where Apple Home really comes in handy. By automating a few of your main lights, you can control them manually from afar, or set randomised schedules that genuinely create the effect of someone moving around the house.

Monitor your home with HomeKit cameras

When I'm travelling, I obviously don't want to be worrying about home the whole time, but I do want to know if anything's happening. In fact, last year I was on the road and a notification let me catch a small issue in time. That's why I trust HomeKit Secure Video so much. I've set up a few cameras outside the house to keep an eye on the surroundings. With HomeKit Secure Video, all footage is stored securely in iCloud+, and since I also use a couple of Apple TVs as hubs, I can easily pull up the live view and recordings from anywhere as long as I have a network connection.

Wrapping up

Summer is a brilliant time to travel, but the extreme heat also means your home needs a bit more looking after. With the right Apple Home setup, you can keep your lawn watered, walk into a nice cool house, run your lights on a varied schedule, and check in on your cameras' live view any time, from anywhere. These are exactly the setups I use when I'm away for work or on a family trip, and they really do take a lot of the stress out of travelling.
